hypothesis: Four gentle code-flow SFT updates followed by Flash-judged RL on a diverse curriculum improve heldout readability, spatial coherence, aesthetics, and executable painting validity.

training.stop_reason: The third five-update window fell below both preceding windows; the reward was bouncing rather than improving consistently.
training.numerical_health: No KL, gradient-norm, or loss instability was observed through update 15.

selected_checkpoint.selection_reason: Latest publicly verified checkpoint available before the early stop.

matched_evaluation.manual_audit: Mixed: some objects and scenes gained contrast or specificity, while other cases lost recognizable structure or object relationships. This does not establish broad heldout improvement.

rollout_forensics.conclusion: The balanced-mixed manifest was not an advancing curriculum. Asynchronous completion, whole-group censorship and cancellation produced uneven family exposure and substantial rollout waste; spatial-pair tasks had the weakest reward signal. A subsequent run needs stratified family sampling, explicit stage advancement, and a judge-uncertainty recovery policy rather than more mixed sampling.

renderer_profile.conclusion: The median is usable, but the approximately 180-second tail caused cancellations and wasted inference work.

utilization.conclusion: Policy inference was saturated; the trainer was not, because it waited for rollout rendering and external judgments.

cost.api_cost: separate and not reconstructed from an invoice

next_decision: Keep the existing Flash12 starting policy as the general checkpoint. Before another paid run, remove the renderer timeout tail and replace balanced-mixed sampling with equal family exposure plus explicit stage advancement, then evaluate that single change on this same matched panel. Do not scale this checkpoint merely because isolated cases improved.
